long_biography.plain_text:
Sent to establish Vitol's Dubai office in 2006, Christopher Bake turned the assignment into a regional origination platform. He helped create Oman Trading International and managed the acquisition of the Fujairah refinery. The work followed roles in Bahrain, Buenos Aires, Houston and London, and led to executive-committee and head-of-origination responsibilities.

Across three decades, Bake's remit widened from commodity trading to infrastructure and downstream governance, including chairmanships at VTTI, Vivo Energy and Petrol Ofisi. He retired from Vitol executive duties in 2024 and later left the VTTI chair. He remains involved with the University of Texas's Global Sustainability Leadership Institute and its multidisciplinary leadership programmes.

uncertainties.detail: Vitol was employee-owned during Bake's tenure, with no individual above five percent in its 2020 disclosure. No public record reviewed identifies whether Bake personally held shares, their size or their redemption on retirement. Executive committee, managing-director and board status are not treated as proof of a personal Vitol stake.

Bake chaired or directed VTTI, Vivo Energy, Petrol Ofisi and other Vitol-related businesses and helped manage the Fujairah refinery acquisition. These were employer or portfolio-company governance roles; none is presented as personal beneficial ownership.

An FCC filing identifies Bake as economic settlor and discretionary beneficiary of the Bake Trust but says he has no voting interest and no right to a fixed percentage of its assets. The filing does not establish that the trust is his principal wealth source or reveal its current composition.

Bake retired from Vitol during 2024 and left VTTI's chair in 2025. Current filings identify a holding partnership and other appointments but do not provide enough business or valuation detail to establish which current private sector predominates; Energy remains a sub-threshold candidate.
